(5) $.config.set on own userConfig untested headless. (6) $.store merges per key across concurrent sessions, no loss in 4 rounds. (7) tasks on disk at ~/.claude/tasks/<sessionId>/<n>.json {id,subject,description,activeForm,status,blocks,blockedBy}. (8) desktop PATH and pane-button prompts need the user (probes/p8-manual.sh).

payload.acceptance_criteria:
- When a mod folder is added under mods/, `npm run marketplace` shall write .claude-plugin/marketplace.json with one entry per mod, its source ./mods/<name> and its plugin.json version.
- When marketplace.json differs from the generator output, `npm run validate` shall fail and name the generate command.
- When a mod lists dependencies in plugin.json, `npm run types` shall load the dependency folders beside it, so its .claude-plugin/types/<dependency>/index.d.ts exists.
- When a dependency's types/index.d.ts is newer than the laid copy, `npm run typecheck` shall lay the types again.
- basicly.toml shall set [worktree] base_branch = "main" and declare marketplace.json under [worktree.regenerate_commands].
- When the session root holds .beads/issues.jsonl with 3 issue lines and 1 tombstone, $.workitems shall publish a snapshot with state ok, source beads and 3 normalized items keyed beads:<id>.
- When no tracker is found at the session root, the snapshot state shall be no-tracker and no parent folder shall be read.
- When a tracker file is over 4 MiB or a line is malformed, the snapshot state shall be failed with a reason that names the file.
- When refresh() runs after a change, it shall return the created, updated and closed items.
- The contract shall ship as mods/workitems/types/index.d.ts with the snapshot, the item, the write-verb table per tracker and the state texts of docs/mocks.md section 0.
- While a refresh runs, a second refresh call shall join it, and the provider shall poll file mtimes with $.clock.every at a minimum interval.

payload.acceptance_criteria:
- When the person runs /task add <text>, task-pane shall call TaskCreate through $.tool.call, append a note that the list changed, and reply as docs/mocks.md shows.
- When the person runs /task add <item id>, the task shall take the work item's title; if workitems cannot read the item, then the reply shall say why by name.
- When the person runs /task rm <n>, task-pane shall call TaskUpdate status=deleted; if no task n exists, then the reply shall list the valid numbers.

payload.value:
- When a mod folder is added under mods/, `npm run marketplace` shall write .claude-plugin/marketplace.json with one entry per mod, its source `./mods/<name>` and its plugin.json version.
- When marketplace.json differs from the generator output, `npm run validate` shall fail and name the generate command.
- When a mod lists dependencies in plugin.json, `npm run types` shall load the dependency folders beside it, so its `.claude-plugin/types/<dependency>/index.d.ts` exists.
- When a dependency's types/index.d.ts is newer than the laid copy, `npm run typecheck` shall lay the types again.

- When refresh() runs after a change, it shall return the created, updated and closed items.
- The contract shall ship as mods/workitems/types/index.d.ts with the snapshot, the item, the write-verb table per tracker and the state texts of docs/mocks.md section 0.
- While a refresh runs, a second refresh call shall join it, and the provider shall poll file mtimes with $.clock.every at a minimum interval.

payload.name: acceptance_criteria
payload.value:
- When the session starts, task-pane shall register the model tools `task_add`, `task_update` and `task_list` through $.tool.register, and add a system prompt section that tells the model to keep its plan in them.
- When the model or the person adds, updates or removes a task, the list in $.state shall change and the pane and `/task` shall show it.
- When the person runs /task add `<text>`, task-pane shall add the task and append a note so the model knows the person changed the list; the reply shall match docs/mocks.md.
- When the person runs /task add `<item id>`, the task shall take the work item title from workitems; if workitems cannot read the item, then the reply shall say why by name.
- When the person runs /task rm `<n>`, task-pane shall remove task n; if no task n exists, then the reply shall list the valid numbers.
- When the session has no tasks, the pane and /task shall list the tracker open items with explicit add buttons and add nothing on their own; an item already a task shall not be added twice.
- When the person runs /task pane, the pane shall open; userConfig mode off, toggle or always shall set the default.
- The list shall reset on session.end with reason clear, and survive a hot reload.

When a tracker item or the model supplies task text, I want task-pane to keep it apart from the person's words, so I can trust that a note marked as mine is mine.

When a session runs tools, I want each tool call drawn as one readable row with what it does and how it ended, so I can follow the work without reading raw commands, JSON and output walls.

- quiet-items keeps the rows of tracker writes; tool-rows must defer to it.

- mods/tool-rows/
- .claude-plugin/marketplace.json
- docs/design.md
- docs/mocks.md

payload.text: Design 2026-10-08: design lane plus Codex second opinion. Agreed: no start time in ToolUse props, so measure around next(e) with the mod clock (it includes approval waits); ToolUse has no ctrl+o signal, so the raw view is the /tool-rows toggle; Bash has no numeric exit code and the error text has no guaranteed format, so parse it when present and else show no code. Corrections from the second opinion: quiet-items ready means initialized, not that it drew a row, so tool-rows must defer by the quiet-items row state of that call, not by the ready key; the Updated file diff placement inside ToolResult needs a live probe. Biggest risk: a short row hides output or a diff with false certainty. Second opinion: build Bash first inside tool-rows, with the engine row for every case it does not cover. Live probes still open: ctrl+o, bashEditDiff placement, exit code text, the clock redraw.

Design 2026-10-08: design lane plus Codex second opinion, both pick a new mod agent-board with its own Pane. Confirmed in the types: tool.call input carries the agentId of a subagent loop; agent.spawn fires for the Agent tool and resolves with an optional agentId; turn.complete carries durationMs and an optional usage; agent.list leaves out workflow agents and drops ended agents; no render component reaches the engine tasks list. Limits: two Panes do not show at once, they become tabs; agent.list history expires, so the mod keeps the rows it saw and marks lost history as unknown; forked-skill agents may appear without agent.spawn. Hot path: the tool.call hook passes main-loop calls straight through and keeps bounded memory per agent; list and render work runs only while the pane is shown. Live probes open: tool.call with agentId from a background subagent, agent.list retention, the hook cost.

payload.name: acceptance_criteria
payload.value:
- When a Bash call finishes with no error, tool-rows shall draw one row with the description, exit 0, the stdout line count and the elapsed time, and shall draw the result row empty.
- When a Bash call errors with an output that starts with Error: Exit code N, the row shall show exit N and the first non-empty line after it.
- When the Bash input has no description, the row shall show the first command segment, cut with an ellipsis.
- While a Bash call runs, the row shall show running and the elapsed time since its tool.call.
- When the Bash output carries bashEditDiff, the row shall show the file count and the added and removed line totals.
- When quiet-items stored a row for the call, tool-rows shall pass the ToolUse and ToolResult renders on unchanged.
- When /tool-rows runs, the mod shall toggle its mode for the session and reply with the new mode; while the mode is off, every row shall draw as the engine draws it.
- If a call is interrupted, refused or a non-Bash tool, or drawing throws, tool-rows shall pass the render on unchanged.

payload.name: acceptance_criteria
payload.value:
- When /agent-board runs, the mod shall open the pane agent-board, and the pane shall show one row per subagent that agent.list returns or that tool.call showed.
- While no subagent exists, the pane shall show No subagents in this session yet.
- When a tool.call with an agentId starts, the row of that agent shall show the tool and its target; when the call resolves, the row shall add 1 to its tool count.
- When a tool.call has no agentId, the mod shall pass it on unchanged and change no row.
- If a hook of the mod throws, then the tool call shall still resolve with the result of next.
- While the pane is shown, the mod shall redraw every second and show the elapsed time since the spawn; when the pane closes, the timer shall stop.
- When a subagent has a parentId, its row shall show under and the parent name or description.
- While every subagent is completed, failed or killed, the header shall read all N done, and the rows shall keep their tool count and time.

payload.value:
- When a Bash call finishes with no error, simple-view shall draw one row with the description, the program, exit 0, the stdout line count and the elapsed time, and shall draw the result as one Updated line per changed file with its added and removed totals, or as nothing when no file changed.
- When a Bash call errors with an output that starts with Error: Exit code N, the row shall show exit N and the first non-empty line after it.
- When the Bash input has no description, the row shall show the first command segment, cut with an ellipsis.
- While a Bash call runs, the row shall show running and the elapsed time since its tool.call.
- When an Edit or Write call succeeds, simple-view shall draw one row with the file path and its added and removed line totals, without the diff body.
- When quiet-items stored a row for the call, simple-view shall pass the ToolUse and ToolResult renders on unchanged.
- When /simple runs, the mod shall toggle its mode for the session, set the quiet-items mode to the same value, and reply with the new mode; while the mode is off, every row shall draw as the engine draws it.
- When /simple show N runs, the mod shall print the full input, output and file diff of the N-th last tool call of the session; when N is out of range, it shall refuse by name and give the valid range.
- If a call is interrupted or refused, or drawing throws, simple-view shall pass the render on unchanged.

When the engine sends no bashEditDiff for a Bash call, I want the row and /simple show N to say that file changes were not tracked, so a write never reads as no change.

- mods/simple-view/hooks/output.ts bashChanges returns isTracked true with zero files when the field is undefined.

## Trigger

When the installed basicly is 0.21.1 or later, I want workitems to stop asking again after each basicly upgrade or kit change, so I can answer the approval once per repo.

## Decision (user, 2026-10-08, second design)

- Ask once, keep the answer. No basicly command runs before approval. After approval the approved program reports its version; on 0.21.1 or later the approval no longer covers the kit files.

payload.text: Result 2026-10-08, Claude Code 2.1.295, live session on tmux -L handily-live, counts from subagent transcripts with jq. Round 1, a 4-step read task, unprompted: 3 Explore and 3 general-purpose subagents made 0 task tool calls (2 tool calls each); the main agent also made 0, so the round could not separate the causes. Round 2, a 9-step build task, unprompted: 3 of 3 general-purpose subagents used the task-pane tools, 7, 9 and 7 calls. All three wrote into the one session list, and Claude Code then suggested the prompt 'clean up the duplicate tasks in the task list'. Not run: Explore on a long task. In this session, two builder subagents told to use the tools also wrote into the main list. Verdict: subagents keep a list when the task is worth planning, so handily-fwkt.8.2 and .8.3 rest on real data; .8.2 is needed now, because the shared list mixes agents.

Result 2026-10-08, Claude Code 2.1.295, scratch mod l0-probe loaded with --plugin-dir in a scratch git repo on tmux -L handily-live; log lines copied from the pane. (1) $.agent.spawn from a command returns an agentId; an agent type registered with isolation worktree runs in .claude/worktrees/agent-<id> on its own branch, and the probe file landed there, not in the main tree. (2) turn.complete reaches the mod with reason=answer and the agent's final text, for background and foreground. (3) Default mode: tool.check gives ask with the subagent agentId, and the dialog 'Bash command · from the l0-probe plugin' reached the person for a background and a foreground agent; Yes ran the call, No made the agent report the denial. (4) Auto mode: tool.check still gives ask, but no dialog appears; the auto mode classifier decides, and SubagentHandback also gets ask with 'requires auto-mode classifier review'. So ask alone does not mean the person must act (input for handily-fwkt.8.10). (5) There is no foreground spawn argument; the mod's agent.spawn hook rewrote background to false and the engine honoured it. (6) The main model got the answers of the 2 agents spawned in auto mode but reported the 2 default-mode agents as never reported back: the hand-back of a mod-spawned agent may not reach the main model in every case; unexplained. Not run: a second background agent in each mode. Verdict: light mode is feasible from a mod: worktree isolation, answers and permission prompts all reach their target.

payload.text: Result 2026-10-08, Claude Code 2.1.295, scratch plugin hook-probe on tmux -L handily-live. (1) A repo with .pre-commit-config.yaml: no question, a refusal that names the manager, no hook written. (2) Inside a mod, git config --get core.hooksPath returns /dev/null although the shell returns nothing: Claude Code disables hooks for the git commands a mod runs. So a mod must not read core.hooksPath or --git-path hooks/pre-commit through its own git calls; read .git/config or use --git-common-dir. With /dev/null ignored the ask appeared once (Not now default, Install for this repo). (3) git rev-parse --git-path hooks/pre-commit gave no usable path inside the mod, so the install failed; the probe still kept the answer install and does not retry: the real mod must keep the answer only after the install works, or reinstall when the hook file is missing. (4) The builder ran the hook in a clone: an unrelated commit passed, a change or delete of an approved test was refused with the file named. (5) Install routes, measured by the builder: npm lefthook 2.2.1 runs from node_modules/.bin with no global install, but its postinstall runs lefthook install in INIT_CWD, so install with --ignore-scripts; uvx pre-commit 4.6.2 needs uv and a uv-managed Python, and uvx pre-commit install writes a uv cache Python path into the hook, which a cache clean breaks. (6) API gaps: $.fs.write has no file mode (chmod needs $.process.run), $.fs has no delete, AskOptions has no default (the first option acts as it), $.plugin has no data folder. Verdict: a plugin can install a test lock with consent; a plain hook script with no hook manager is the most robust route.

payload.value:
- When the main loop calls a tool other than the task tools, the pane shows under the task in progress its last tool and target, the count of tool calls since that task started, and the time since it started.

- A click on a task shows its full title, its start time and its tool count under the row, and a second click hides them.
- The pane lists each running subagent with its plan count from task-pane state and its last tool, and lists no subagent section when none runs.
- When the main loop keeps no task list, the pane shows a Now line with the last tool and target, the count per tool, and the time since the first tool call.
- After 20 main loop tool calls with no task list, or with no task update since the last 20 calls, the pane shows a warning with the count and a button that puts a plan request into the prompt box without sending it.
- When that warning holds as the person submits a prompt, the mod adds one context note that asks Claude to keep its plan with task_add and task_update, at most once per 20 tool calls, and never blocks the prompt.
- The README describes the pane as built, the version is 0.4.0, and npm run check passes.

## Trigger

When workitems reads a basicly tracker on a slow host, I want to see the items within the hook time limit, so I can use the panes on Windows.

## Evidence

- Report 2026-10-09: one refresh starts 6 basicly processes; on Windows the host reports 'HooksError: $.workitems.refresh: workitems did not answer within 10000ms' on every poll.
- readers/basicly.ts:141-152 runs approvedProgram (approval check, and with a changed kit basicly --version) once per status in OPEN_STATUSES, then tracker list per status.
- Measured here: a basicly call takes 240 to 470 ms warm; a full list of the basicly ledger is 8,631,564 bytes, over the 4 MiB cap, so the per-status lists stay.

payload.title: reply-view: condensed tables with wrapped cells, buttons on the header row, and a fold after 30 lines

payload.name: acceptance_criteria
payload.value:
- A table that does not fit the width wraps its long cells inside their columns, and draws one block per row only below 40 columns.
- The copy and copy as text buttons sit on the header row of a table, so a table takes no extra line for them.
- copy as text gives plain text with no markdown marks, no pipes and no escapes, that pastes into an email or a chat as written.
- A reply folds only when it is longer than 30 lines.
- npm run check passes, and a live check at 80 and 120 columns shows each case.

payload.name: description
payload.value:
## Trigger

When Claude answers with a table, I want to see it condensed and readable, and copy it into an email or a chat with no formatting artifacts, so I can reuse the answer without editing it.

## Evidence

- Screenshots 2026-10-09: a 4-column table with long cells drew as label and value blocks, about 45 lines; a 5-row table drew as about 20 lines; each table adds a line for [ copy ] [ copy as text ].
- Probe 2026-10-09 (tmux frames every 100 ms, reply-view 0.2.0): the engine draws its own box table while a reply streams (f026-f058) and the hook's tree only at completion (f059). The jump is engine-side; feedback drafted. The person chose to keep the conversion and to fold only after 30 lines.

payload.title: simple-view: one row for Read, Grep and Glob, the error before the cut, no time under one second, and a spike on grouped calls

payload.name: acceptance_criteria
payload.value:
- A Read, Grep or Glob call draws one row with the tool, the target relative to the session root, and the line or match count.
- An error row keeps the description and cuts the error text first.
- A Bash row shows no time under one second.
- A spike of at most one hour records whether a ui.render hook can draw the calls inside the engine ToolGroup, and the result is written to this record.
- npm run check passes, and a live check shows each row.

## Trigger

When Claude reads and searches files, I want to see each call as one short row, so I can follow the work without long engine rows.

payload.name: description
payload.value:
## Trigger

When Claude runs a tool call, I want to see the mod row from the start, so I can follow the work without 1 to 2 seconds of raw engine output.

## Evidence

- Frame probe 2026-10-09 (100 ms frames, simple-view 0.4.0): the engine group line 'Running 1 shell command…' showed for about 0.7 s, then 'Bash(sleep 2; seq 1 5)' for about 0.5 s, before the mod row; a Read showed the engine 'Read' row for about 0.3 s.
- ToolUse props carry the tool name and an input that streams in; no flag marks the input complete, so the mod returns next(e) until it can read the input.
